named_subject: a pig seen from the side, facing left, with a spiral snout, two pointed ears, a round body and four stick legs
action: The pig stands still for the first six frames, then drifts left and down while its body grows larger and rounder, as if stepping toward the viewer, but it stays in side profile throughout.
identity_gap: Frames 1 to 12 match the doodle's zigzag ears, square spiral snout and stick legs, but from frame 14 on the back ear is replaced by a tall straight vertical line and the head outline swells, so the drawing no longer reads as the same pig.
notes: The film shows the pig turning from side profile to a three-quarter front view as it walks toward the camera, while the drawing never turns and only shifts and inflates, with jumps in position at frames 8-9 and a sudden head drop and ear loss at 13-14. The one change that would help most is keeping the two-point zigzag ear shape fixed on the head in every frame so the late frames stay the same drawing, then easing the position change between frames 8-9 and 12-14.
